links.outcome: Residents' accuracy and sensitivity in detecting AI-generated hallucinations in ChatGPT answers
links.effect: Mean accuracy 55% ± 4.3%; mean d' 0.39 ± 0.33; residents struggled to identify AI errors, particularly in clinical cases.
links.quote: The mean (SD) accuracy was 55% ±4.3%, and the mean (SD) sensitivity (d') was 0.39 ± 0.33.

links.outcome: Whether users detect incorrect AI outputs
links.effect: Residents had low error detection accuracy (55%) and low sensitivity (d' 0.39), indicating poor detection of incorrect AI outputs.
links.quote: The study concluded that residents struggled to identify AI errors, particularly in clinical cases, emphasizing the importance of improving AI literacy and critical thinking for effective integration into medical education.

unlisted_practices: AI literacy education and critical thinking training for medical residents

screen.reason: Empirically tests the ability of general practice residents to detect AI-generated hallucinations/errors (measuring the effectiveness of human-in-the-loop / clinician review of generative AI outputs).
